content.user_title: Resolve GitHub Issues With Team Workflow
content.value_statement: Issue work often stalls when investigation, fixes, tests, and pull requests are handled separately. This skill guides a structured workflow from triage to verification.
actual_capabilities: Guides issue triage with severity labels, missing context checks, and linked work review.
Outlines branch strategy, commit grouping, and pull request preparation for issue-based work.
Provides root cause analysis steps using repository history, reproduction, and related issue review.
Recommends unit, integration, end-to-end, lint, and type-check verification before review.
Structures pull request summaries, test evidence, closure comments, and rollback notes.
limitations: Requires repository access, GitHub permissions, and project-specific commands from the user.
Does not replace human code review, product judgment, or release approval.
Cannot guarantee that CI passes or that a proposed fix is accepted.
Example commands must be adapted to the repository policies and tooling.

use_cases.title: Triage incoming bug reports
use_cases.description: Maintainers can classify severity, gather missing context, and find related issues before assigning implementation work.

use_cases.title: Implement verified fixes
use_cases.description: Engineers can move from reproduction to root cause, tests, code changes, and pull request evidence.

use_cases.title: Coordinate release follow-up
use_cases.description: Technical leads can plan verification, deployment monitoring, closure comments, and rollback notes for critical issues.

prompt_templates.title: Start Issue Triage
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner triage for a new issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill for GitHub issue #123. Summarize the report, classify priority, list missing context, and suggest next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Bug Fix
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan a fix for issue #123. Include likely root causes, files to inspect, tests to add, and branch naming.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a Pull Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to prepare the pull request for issue #123. Draft the summary, testing evidence, risk notes, and reviewer checklist.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Critical Resolution
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill for a critical production issue. Create a triage plan, hotfix workflow, verification checklist, communication plan, and rollback notes.

output_examples.input: A bug report says login fails after token expiry.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a triage summary, reproduction plan, likely root cause areas, test targets, implementation steps, and pull request guidance.

output_examples.input: A feature request needs profile customization with backend and frontend changes.
output_examples.output: The skill breaks the request into phases, suggests ownership boundaries, identifies tests, and prepares review-ready delivery notes.

output_examples.input: A slow query issue affects a high-traffic page.
output_examples.output: The skill guides measurement, query investigation, optimization validation, regression tests, deployment checks, and rollback planning.

best_practices: Start with issue facts, reproduction steps, linked work, and clear acceptance criteria.
Add tests that prove the fix and protect the affected workflow from regressions.
Include concise pull request evidence, verification steps, and known risks for reviewers.
anti_patterns: Starting code changes before confirming the expected behavior and reproduction path.
Closing issues without test evidence, reviewer context, or a clear pull request reference.
Copying example commands without adapting them to repository tooling and permissions.

faq.question: Does this skill require GitHub CLI access?
faq.answer: No, but many examples use GitHub CLI. Users can adapt the workflow to browser or API-based issue management.

faq.question: Can it fix issues automatically?
faq.answer: It can guide investigation, implementation, tests, and pull request preparation. The user still controls repository changes and approvals.

faq.question: Is it only for bugs?
faq.answer: No. It also supports feature requests, performance work, release follow-up, and documentation updates tied to issues.

faq.question: Does it choose the final priority?
faq.answer: It suggests priority using impact, severity, and workaround signals. Team policy should decide the final classification.

faq.question: Can it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow is written for agent-assisted development across Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What inputs produce the best results?
faq.answer: Provide the issue URL, repository context, expected behavior, reproduction notes, test commands, and project constraints.
